t: You're standing on Keats Grove, a quiet residential street in Hampstead. It takes its name from John Keats, the English Romantic poet. He belonged to the second generation of Romantic poets, alongside Byron and Shelley. His poems had been published for less than four years when he died of tuberculosis at twenty-five. They were indifferently received while he lived, but his fame grew rapidly afterwards. By the end of the century he was part of the canon of English literature, and his Ode to a Nightingale was being called one of the final masterpieces.
